note: Tier 1 is the infrastructure floor: transaction-only bootstrap of the seven successor artifacts on a fresh localhost ledger, through infrastructure init, Loader-v3 revocation, per-role immutable release activation, bounded Registry record and Product-graph publication, the Market-scoped LifecycleRentCreditV2, and canonical Core Found37 — plus every hostile case the runner submits. These bindings are authored by the GAUNTLET, never by the campaign, so that a label change breaks loudly instead of quietly dropping coverage. `program: ""` with `routes: []` is the explicit form for a transaction that drives no dClutch route: an airdrop, a Loader SetAuthority, an SPL Token-2022 call, an Address Lookup Table call.

bindings.label: fund *
bindings.note: Faucet airdrops to the ephemeral Core authority and the hostile authority. No dClutch program is invoked.

bindings.label: wrong authority cannot initialize infrastructure
bindings.note: HOSTILE. A wrong signer attempts the sole Core infrastructure-profile initialization. Refuses Infrastructure (0x300F) — 'Core bootstrap profile, artifact, Loader, or immutability authority refused' — which is the right refusal for a wrong immutability authority. The runner additionally asserts that no profile account exists afterwards.

bindings.label: initialize Core infrastructure profile
bindings.note: Creates the sole Core-owned Registry/Rent ProtocolInfrastructureProfileV1 PDA. Not genesis-injected: this is a submitted transaction, and the profile's exact body is cross-checked by a witness.

bindings.label: immutable release activation refuses pre-revocation Core
bindings.note: HOSTILE. Core still carries an upgrade authority, so it is not an immutable release and activation must refuse. The runner asserts no activation cache account is left behind.

bindings.label: revoke Core Loader-v3 upgrade authority
bindings.note: Agave Loader v3 SetAuthority(Some -> None). No dClutch program is invoked; the poststate bytes are pinned by a witness.

bindings.label: activate immutable release-set role: *
bindings.note: One transaction per ExecutionRoleV1. Five of them: whole-ELF hashing makes a single five-role activation exceed the compute maximum outright (see the activation-is-one-role-per-transaction witness).

bindings.label: late activation substitution rolls back prior transfer
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the strongest rollback case in tier 1: a lamport transfer is placed FIRST in the same transaction as an activation whose role ProgramData coordinate has been substituted. Refuses Deployment (0x1003) — 'Loader Program, ProgramData, linkage, slot, ELF, or authority refused' — which is exactly the substituted coordinate. The runner asserts the recipient account does not exist afterwards and that the payer's delta is EXACTLY the transaction fee: byte-exact rollback, not merely 'it failed'.

bindings.label: create immutable Token-2022 collateral plus explicit local participant fixture liquidity
bindings.note: SPL Token-2022 InitializeMint2 / InitializeAccount3 / MintTo / SetAuthority(None). A real mint with real decimals, not a fixture: raw u64 atoms are preserved and the decimals field is treated as display metadata only. The mint authority is revoked in the same transaction, which is what makes the collateral immutable, and the local participant's fixture liquidity is minted before that revocation because afterwards nobody can.

bindings.label: publish record: Begin *
bindings.note: DCLTRIX1 action 1. Allocates the exact raw record account and its temporary staging cursor.

bindings.label: publish record: Append *
bindings.note: DCLTRIX1 action 2. Appends the cursor-selected next semantic page. The next action is derived from finalized chain state each round, never from a client-held plan.

bindings.label: publish record: Finalize *
bindings.note: DCLTRIX1 action 3. Authenticates the complete raw bytes and closes the cursor.

bindings.label: publish record: substituted refund wallet refuses
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The Finalize refund-wallet coordinate is replaced with an attacker-chosen address; the cursor's rent must not be redirectable.

bindings.label: publish Product graph: *Begin
bindings.note: The Runtime-V2 Product root, result domain and portfolio are published through one chain-derived graph state machine. Each member's record still goes through the ordinary Begin/Append/Finalize route.

bindings.label: publish Product graph: *Append
bindings.note: As above, the Append step of a Product graph member.

bindings.label: publish Product graph: *Finalize
bindings.note: As above, the Finalize step of a Product graph member.

bindings.label: create * routing address lookup table
bindings.note: Solana Address Lookup Table program. Routing is table data, never protocol authority: only non-signer coordinates and the invoked program are routed, the fee payer and every signer stay in the message's static key list, and the table is authority-owned so its rent stays recoverable.

bindings.label: extend * routing table page *
bindings.note: Address Lookup Table ExtendLookupTable. No dClutch program is invoked.

bindings.label: create Market-scoped lifecycle RentCreditV2
bindings.note: DCLRNCI2 Create. The Market and Market+generation credit PDAs are projected from one same-slot finalized snapshot, then the credit is created and reacquired finalized.

bindings.label: Found37 refuses substituted lifecycle credit
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The lifecycle rent-credit coordinate is substituted. Refuses AccountFrame (0x3001) — 'account count, order, privilege, executable flag, or alias refused' — at 6,958 CU, before any protocol work: the substitution collides with another frame coordinate and the alias check catches it first. Recorded here rather than assumed: the refusal a hostile case ACTUALLY raises is a fact about the program, not a preference.

bindings.label: Found37 refuses a substituted Market coordinate and rolls the transaction back
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the sharpest one: a substituted Market coordinate under attacker-chosen address-lookup-table routing, in a multi-instruction transaction that must roll back to a fee-only debit. Refuses RentCredit (0x3006) — 'RentCredit owner, bytes, PDA, or persisted beneficiary refused'. Worth reading carefully: the Market substitution is caught by the rent-credit-to-Market PDA binding, not by a Market check, because the lifecycle credit is a PDA of [domain, market, generation]. Substituting the Market therefore breaks the credit's derivation before anything looks at the Market itself.

bindings.label: create canonical Found37 Market
bindings.note: The canonical Core Found37, submitted as a v0 transaction over a finalized address lookup table because the frame does not fit a legacy packet with its keys inline. This is the route that ~2,300 unit tests could not tell you had never been submitted.

bindings.label: create the founding generation's lifecycle RentCreditV2
bindings.note: The generic founding runs at its own generation against a Market that does not exist yet, so it needs its own Market-scoped LifecycleRentCreditV2. Its refund wallet is the founding's beneficiary, which Core's Found stage requires to equal the artifact's own `beneficiary`.

bindings.label: DCLTPCB2 refuses a non-terminal projected-Custody request
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The bootstrap admits exactly one request: the terminal LockHoardAndCloseSource its founding artifact determines. A well-formed but NON-TERMINAL prestate request in that slot refuses in `decode_projected_request`, before any CPI and nowhere near the allocator.

bindings.label: DCLTPCB2 refuses a reordered FundingLedgerV2 tail and rolls the transaction back
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The two FundingLedgerV2 accounts are the manifest binding: Resolution owns the exact 0b0111 subset and Trading owns the exact 0b1000 subset. Swapping them breaks that canonical controller partition and the artifact's ordered `funding_list_id` join. The whole bootstrap must roll back with neither ledger nor any projected-Custody account left behind, and the runner asserts a fee-only debit.

bindings.label: stage projected custody against prepared controller funding (DCLTPCB2)
bindings.note: Projected Custody in one rollback domain against a Market that does not exist: Initialize (with Core's ProjectFound37 projection CPI), OpenHoard, OpenSourceCompartment, staged against the controller funding ledgers DCLTCFQ1 already prepared. The transaction carries ComputeBudget::RequestHeapFrame, and the route presents the instructions sysvar its entrypoint adapter uses to re-derive that grant. The two FundingLedgerV2 accounts moved OUT of this transaction when the founding was split; the Resolution CPI that created them moved with them, and so did the Registry reauthentication.

bindings.label: pre-fund the founding's program-allocated accounts
bindings.note: One System transfer per program-allocated account (the founding escrow joined them in 266c1d687, and the label stopped counting). Core allocates the Market and the one-shot founding permit and Claims allocates the aggregate, the founder Position, and the admission with `allocate` and `assign` only, never a transfer, so each must already hold its rent. The Market and the permit are compared for EXACT equality with their rent minima, and all three Claims balances are folded byte-exactly into the Claims request Core commits to inside the permit.

bindings.label: DCLTGMF3 refuses a substituted Claims request and rolls the whole founding back
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the one this campaign existed to reach. The substituted readonly Claims request record names a DIFFERENT FOUNDER and is otherwise byte-identical, so the Position and the admission it would mint belong to somebody else. The outer's cross-request join is the only thing between that record and a stolen Position; it refuses before its first CPI, and the refusal has to take Lock, Found, Realize, and Claims with it. The runner asserts a fee-only debit and that all five allocated accounts are still vacant.

bindings.label: found the Market atomically: Lock, Found, Realize, Claims, Open (DCLTGMF3)
bindings.note: The first Open Market. Five stages in one rollback domain and one transaction: Custody LockHoardAndCloseSource, Core Found-and-permit, Custody RealizeAndClose, Claims FoundingV5, and Core Open LAST so that any late refusal rolls the whole chain back. It creates the Market, mints the liability aggregate, the founder Position, and the admission, moves the collateral into the Hoard, closes the source compartment, realizes the projection into the Market's normal Custody replay, and consumes the one-shot permit.

bindings.label: freeze * routing table after its one complete extension plan
bindings.note: Address Lookup Table FreezeLookupTable. No dClutch program is invoked. A frozen table cannot be extended or closed, so the routing a founding was submitted over is fixed for the life of the ledger -- which is what makes the pre-mutation compiled-message lock census the campaign prints comparable with the post-routing one.

bindings.label: prepare exact controller funding ledgers and checkpoint (DCLTCFQ1)
bindings.note: The controller-funding half of what DCLTPCB1 used to do in one transaction. Trading prepares both FundingLedgerV2 accounts -- the Resolution-owned 0b0111 subset through a release-authenticated Resolution CPI, which itself projects Core's Found to authenticate the Market it is funding, and the Trading-owned 0b1000 subset -- plus the controller-funding checkpoint that DCLTCF1A and DCLTPCB2 both read. Splitting it out is why the founding fits its packet at all.

bindings.label: DCLTCF1A refuses to close the first controller ledger before checkpoint expiry
bindings.note: HOSTILE. The controller-funding cleanup exists so a prepared-but-abandoned funding can be unwound; while its checkpoint has not expired the founding is still satisfiable and the ledgers may not be destroyed. Refuses Content (0x4003) at 8,453 CU, before any CPI. Content is this program's coarse code with 2,126 sites, so this row pins the CODE and not the conjunct -- the conjunct rides sol_log on the refusing path and naming it here would be a claim this campaign cannot check.

bindings.label: core-funding-create-v1
bindings.note: The first rung of the post-founding readiness ladder Core's resolution.rs states: Found, then CreateFund, then VerifyFundReady. Core writes the prepaid Source destination and CPIs Resolution to create the fund. Reached for the first time on 2026-09-03, because it is the transaction AFTER the founding and the founding did not complete before then.

bindings.label: resolution-funding-activate-v1
bindings.note: The second rung: Resolution activates the pending funds it was told to create. Resolution alone -- no Core CPI -- which is why the ladder needs a third transaction to move Core's readiness.

bindings.label: core-funding-accept-v1
bindings.note: The third rung, and the one that moves the Market's readiness to Ready. Core alone: it reads the activated funding and accepts it. This is the last transaction tier 1 submits.

bindings.label: reauthenticate the activated role: *
bindings.note: One transaction per ExecutionRoleV1, immediately after the five activations and read back off the chain at a slot no earlier than theirs. This is the route every role adapter's rule is WRITTEN in and none of them can call: a child entered under a Registry continuation cannot CPI back here, the Registry is already on the stack, so the adapters share `process_reauthenticate`'s body rather than reimplementing it. That makes this the one place the shared rule is exercised as a route instead of as a subroutine -- and until 2026-09-03 nothing anywhere had submitted it, while `docs/design/PACKET_LIMIT_2026_09_01.md` listed it among the routes tier 1 drives. It could not share a frame with the activation that precedes it: `build_registry_reauthentication_v1` is handed a finalized observation of the cache and refuses a role the cache does not yet carry.

bindings.label: Abort refuses a substituted sponsor refund wallet
bindings.note: HOSTILE, and the boundary this route is judged on. The staging cursor is the SOLE author of the sponsor refund identity; a frame naming a stranger's wallet must die on that comparison before a lamport moves, and the record must survive being refused for. An unwind route that let anyone redirect a sponsor's refund would be a worse defect than the stranding Abort was written to prevent. The code is COARSE -- `RegistryError::Record` covers every conjunct in `record_v1`, the substituted refund wallet among them -- so this pins the wall and not the conjunct, which is the honest reading and is stated rather than implied.

bindings.label: reclaim an abandoned record's rent and staging bounty (Abort)
bindings.note: DCLTRIX1 action 4, and the campaign's only use of the record family's liveness guarantee: an abandoned record set can always be reclaimed and never strands its rent or its prepaid bounty. The record this closes exists to be abandoned -- it is published by a Begin, never appended to, never finalized, and carries a schema id that names itself and belongs to no family. Early sponsor Abort: the actor IS the committed sponsor, so the contract requires its signature, the disclosed bounty is withheld (it funds a STRANGER's later cleanup, not the sponsor's own abort), and both closed accounts' whole balance returns to one wallet. The producer checks that arithmetic against the chain rather than asserting it in a witness.
